To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed STTC schemes, based on SC-QICs with optimal and also sub-optimal decoding algorithms in conjunction with OSTBCs, can be used for wireless semi-femtocell MISO and MIMO systems to achieve the lowest possible BEPs.

The performance of the STTCs based on the SC-QICs with optimal and suboptimal decoding schemes in conjunction with the OSTBCs is better than the STTCs with the optimal and suboptiml decoding schemes in conjunction without the OSTBCs.

the STTCs based on the proposed SC-QICs with the optimal and suboptimal decoding methods have a significant improvement in terms of BEP performance over the STTCs with conventional QICs and also over the STTC based on the QICs with a suboptimal decoding algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects.

the following issues: (1) the performance analysis of STTCs based on SC-QICs in conjunction with OSTBCs, and (2) the performance comparison of STTCs with and without SC-QICs, in conjunction with OSTBSCs, and also the performance comparison of the STTCs based SC-QICs with and without the optimal and suboptimal decoding methods, and the STTCs with the optimal decoding algorithm in conjunction with OSTBsCs.
the performance of the STTCs in conjunction with OSTBCs for wireless MISO, and MIMO systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the proposed SC-QICs based STTCs with the suboptimal decoding algorithm, in conjunction with the OSTBCs is very close to that of the optimal decoding algorithm.
the STTCs based SC-QICs in conjunction with OSTBCs have been proved to be a promising candidate technology to achieve the best performance of BEPs and bit/symbol rates for wireless femtocell systems.
the proposed SC-QICs-OSTBCs based semi-femtocell MISO and MIMO schemes can achieve a significant improvement in the BEPs and the bit/symbol capacity compared to the state-of-the-arts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed scheme has shown the ability to provide a better performance than the conventional STTCs in the MISO semi-femtocell systems.
the proposed STTCs based on SC-QICs with the optimal decoding algorithm in conjunction with OSTBCs have the best performance among the other proposed systems in terms of BEP.

the proposed system has shown significant performance gains in terms of the BEPs and also symbol capacity in bandwidth limited error-proneness of wireless channels in comparison to the existing techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by applying the powerful STTCs in conjunction with the OSTBCs, it is possible to reduce the number of transmit antennas and hence, to reduce the complexity, size and cost of the transmitter and receiver sides of a wireless communication system.

, the proposed semi-femtocell MISO/MIMO systems employing STTCs based on SC-QICs with OSTBCs, can achieve significant BEP enhancement and capacity improvement in comparison with the conventional MIMO system with STBCs.

the proposed STTCs based on SC-QICs with the suboptimal decoding algorithm outperform the STTCs based SC-QICs using the optimal decoding scheme, and also STTCs based QICs with the optimal decoding algorithm in the presence of channel estimation errors, and also channel fading effects in the wireless semi-femtocell propagation environment.
